Variants.Content: Golden Tree City is an inland castle in the Reach. Its name retains the shadow of the Gardener Dynasty and the Reach Orchard culture. Trees, orchards and fertile soil make the area part of Highgarden's food system; trees also provide wood, shade, honey and fruit for winemaking. The families of the Reach like to depict themselves in roses, oaks, and gold, but it is the generations of farmers, gardeners, millers, and coachmen who truly maintain the glory of their heraldry. The roads in Golden Tree City connect the surrounding estates and the hinterland of Highgarden. They are cargo routes in peacetime, but they are changed by food requisitions, garrisons and refugees in times of war. Its fixed significance lies in the farm economy and the memory of the Reach's old dynasty, not in any future flag.

Entry Goldengrove They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the Reach; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hooves.

Entry Goldengrove If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

From workshops to sanctuaries, Golden Tree City juxtaposes stone walls, wooden beams, iron gates, tombs and seams repaired by generations with memories of family origins from the days of the Seven Gods, knight legends and the Gardener King. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Goldengrove They care about grain, wine, orchards, pastures and markets along the Mander River. They also look at whether seeds are left after the grain collection and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
